newsitem.title: UK: BA ground staff say yes to 2-yr pay freeze.
newsitem.headline: BA ground staff say yes to 2-yr pay freeze.

text.p: British Airways said on Thursday that around 2,800 ground staff at London's Heathrow Airport had agreed to a two-year pay freeze in return for a commitment by the company to protect jobs into the next century.

British Airways said members of the Transport and General Workers' Union's (T&G) ground services staff voted "overwhelmingly" in favour of a three year proposal which will bring BA's costs into line with its competitors.
Apart from a two-year pay freeze, the staff have agreed on lower starter rates for recruits and promised "best practices" throughout the department.
The staff include ramp and baggage workers and staff whno operate crew and passenger buses.
"Today's agreement marks the successful conclusion of discussions lasting four months between local managers and staff to find savings of 20 million stg within the department," BA said.
This is a part of the airlines efficiency programme which would generate one billion stg of efficiencies before the turn of the century.
